Systems Design & Architecture

Project Midnight

Engineering a modular, data-driven abilities framework and extensible AI behavior state machines in Unity.

Role Technical Designer
Timeline 3 Months (2026)
Engine / Tech Unity / C#
Team Size 4 Developers

Project Overview

Project Midnight is a fast-paced, top-down rogue-like action game built around intense player ability combinations. As the sole technical designer on the team, my responsibility was to design and implement a flexible system capable of handling hundreds of mechanical variations without generating spaghetti code.

The Design Challenge

Our content design team needed to rapidly prototype and balance over 50 unique combat modifications during testing cycles. The naive approach—writing hard-coded scripts for every single spell iteration—clogged our pipeline and created massive development friction between engineering and art asset drops.

"How do we allow designers to configure multi-stage gameplay abilities entirely inside the engine inspector without needing explicit engineering support for every pass?"

The Architecture Solution

I developed a decoupled framework leveraging Unity's data containers. Spells were split down into atomic, reusable actions like applying damage, tracking momentum variables, and instantiating custom particles.

By linking modular actions inside a master container script, team members could drag-and-drop structural elements together to build custom behaviors immediately.

// ScriptableObject action layer example
[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "Abilities/Actions/Damage")]
public class DealDamageAction : AbilityAction
{
    public override void Execute(GameObject user, GameObject target)
    {
        var health = target.GetComponent<IHealth>();
        health?.TakeDamage(damageAmount);
    }
}

The Results

The architecture successfully decoupled system configuration from underlying systems logic. Testing feedback cycles accelerated by roughly 40%, leaving the engineering team free to focus entirely on platform performance bottlenecks and pathfinding systems optimization.

Key Contributions

  • Engineered modular spell infrastructure
  • Authored custom inspector UI tools
  • Optimized state machine updates
